text:
Nora: Heads up — after the telemetry-proxy update at ~12:05 UTC the latency panel for API routes is showing no p95/p99 lines, only p50 and p90. Can someone confirm?
Sam: I see that too on org view (org=acme). Dashboard time range 30m. p95/p99 series are blank.
Priya: Is this global or just a subset of panels? I can't repro on the vanity dashboard.
Nora: Looks global for the 'latency by route' panel. Customer complaint just came in.
Tomas: eng-metrics-bot just flagged ingest lag during the deploy, could be related. eng-metrics-bot: ingestion_lag_seconds avg=188.2 over last 10m :warning: 
Sam: If ingestion lag is elevated, our percentile aggregates could be missing tail buckets. Priya, can you check the metrics-collector logs on canary?
Priya: Checking now. `kubectl -n metrics logs deploy/telemetry-proxy-canary --since=15m` shows a bunch of `Error: partial write: series too wide` warnings starting at 12:03.
Sam: That aligns with the deploy. Could be the proxy dropping high-latency histograms (tails).
eng-metrics-bot: alert: telemetry-proxy-error-rate > 2% for 5m (canary)
Nora: Quick mitigations? Rollback canary? Or switch query to use raw histograms if we have them?
Tomas: My recommendation: first capture a reproducible query that should return p99 and see raw series. Run the direct aggregation from Clickhouse: `SELECT route, quantileTDigest(0.99)(latency_ms) FROM traces WHERE org='acme' AND ts > now() - interval '15' minute GROUP BY route;`
Priya: Ran that against clickhouse, result: many routes returned `NULL` for 0.99. 0.50 and 0.90 returned values. Looks like tails were not ingested into aggregated t-digest shards.
Sam: That suggests the proxy/transform lost high-value samples or the histogram bucketing changed shape. Any recent transform config change?
Priya: The telemetry-proxy update included a PR that changed `histogram_merge_mode` default from `full` to `sketch` to save payload size. PR: https://git.internal/r/telemetry/2345
Nora: Oh — that would drop detailed tail info for merged histograms. Why was this flipped on for canary?
Tomas: The flip was intended to be gated by a feature flag but the env var was mis-set in the canary helm values. I'm rolling a patch to re-enable `full` merge mode on canary now.
Sam: Good call. After the patch, we should trigger a re-ingest for the 5–20 minute window or mark those minutes as partial in the dashboard.
eng-metrics-bot: action: started rollback of telemetry-proxy-canary to v1.12.4 by @Tomas
Priya: Patch applied and canary restarted at 12:22. Logs show no further `series too wide` and ingestion_lag_seconds trending down.
Nora: Can someone confirm the dashboard after the next scrape? I'll tell the customer we're investigating and will update in 15m.
Sam: Re-ran the clickhouse t-digest query at 12:35 — p99 values reappeared for most routes. `SELECT ... quantileTDigest(0.99)` now returns numbers. Dashboard p95/p99 lines still empty for the 12:00–12:25 window (expected) but current time shows lines again.
Tomas: We'll follow up with a postmortem and add an observability test that asserts p99 non-null for high-volume routes after deploy. Also adding a helm guard to prevent changing `histogram_merge_mode` without a feature-toggle.
Nora: Thanks. For the customer: root cause = telemetry-proxy config change in canary that used a lighter histogram merge mode, which lost tail samples during the deploy window; rollback restored tails.
Priya: Filing support ticket with timeline + query snippets for CS to share. Ticket: SUP-4821.
Sam: Postmortem assigned to eng-metrics & eng-release. I'll slack the on-call to review the helm defaults.
Nora: Closing thread for now, reopen if we see reappearance. :thumbsup:
